column3: The Hebrew has both “spoke” and “saying”; BSB condenses these to “said.”
The Hebrew repeats the making verb for the trumpets and their hammered workmanship; BSB gives a single making command.
The Hebrew uses active plural “they shall blow”; BSB uses passive “both are sounded.”
The Hebrew uses active plural “they shall blow” and calls the leaders heads of “the thousands of Israel”; BSB uses a passive verb and calls these groups “clans.”
The Hebrew names a singular alarm blast without an explicit adjective for its length; BSB says “short blasts.”

The Hebrew names a singular alarm blast for each sounding and changes from “you shall blow” to “they shall blow”; BSB uses plural “short blasts” and then makes the blasts the subject signaling departure.
The Hebrew distinguishes blowing from sounding an alarm without explicit length adjectives; BSB specifies “long blasts” and “short ones.”
